reason: E2 shows that 0.25 wt % Y2O3 in CrMnFeCoNi improves room-temperature wear resistance without affecting friction, but it provides no evidence for high-temperature glaze formation, adaptive friction mechanisms, or performance above room temperature. E1 demonstrates adaptive glaze formation and ultralow wear in a different alloy system (Ni50(AlNbTiV)50) without Y2O3, so it does not directly support the claim that Y2O3 nanoparticles enable this mechanism in CoCrFeNi. The key premises about high-temperature behavior and the specific nanoparticle-mediated mechanisms are therefore largely unsupported
premises: Y2O3 nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed in a CoCrFeNi HEA matrix at 0.25–0.5 wt %
Y2O3 nanoparticles will act as nucleation sites for nano-coupled grain structures and promote a nanocrystalline glaze layer
The nanoparticles will reduce room-temperature friction by impeding dislocations and promoting stable shear localization
The nanoparticles will catalyze tribochemical reactions to form a protective glaze layer at high temperatures
The intervention will yield 1–2 orders of magnitude lower wear rate and low friction across RT–800 °C
